observations: Godin & Thivierge PLOS Computational Biology 2026 explicitly expose S1 Code.zip and clarify that principal-angle increases in unconstrained networks should be interpreted as deviations from the initial dominant activity subspace rather than proof of a literally rotating structural manifold.

Courellis et al. Nature Human Behaviour 2026 recorded 970 single neurons in 25 neurosurgical patients and found context coding can be static in medial frontal cortex but dynamic in hippocampus; when context had to be inferred as a latent variable, hippocampal coding became static. This supports a design distinction between a comparatively stable semantic-context anchor and other drifting representations, without directly validating the present controller.
public_source_update.split_code_recovery: Read-only recovery retried. The public PLOS article exposes the S1 Code DOI/link, but the current transport still did not yield file-level ZIP contents. No mutation/probe side effect was used.

bounded_audit.status: full_online_age_expanded_filter_and_tracker_coupling_completed; prototype-permutation identifiability is the dominant unresolved boundary; non_reproduction

design.scope: Synthetic bounded causal control extending the prior event-level identity-anchored duration audit. Not a reproduction of SPLiT, Bruijns et al., or Courellis et al.
design.filter: Online age-expanded semi-Markov posterior with jointly inferred event boundaries. Normal transitions into either cause state; cause states return to normal. Event observations are emitted from cause-specific prediction/emission prototypes that can drift and cross.
models: fixed_hsmm: fixed state-specific duration priors and fixed event-type prior, adaptive emission prototypes
duration_blind_hmm: geometric event durations, adaptive event-type prior and prototypes
capped_fixed_duration: fixed duration evidence capped toward a pooled geometric/base hazard
identity_anchored_adaptive_duration: event-boundary duration updates gated by prototype separation/cause confidence, with pooled-hazard shrinkage under weak identity
oracle: true time-varying duration/prior/prototypes, still performing online state inference
nonstationarity: mixed duration swap + prototype crossing + prior shift
design.heldout_filter_eval: 8 held-out seeds per scenario, 1600 steps/seed. Paired bootstrap confidence intervals are over seed-level differences and are exploratory because n=8.
design.duration_recovery_probe: Separate 12-seed abrupt-swap probe measured recovery of the inferred duration ordering.
design.prototype_permutation_test: A symmetric 3-state HSMM with equal S/C entry prior was evaluated under simultaneous S/C prototype and duration-label permutation. Forward log-marginal likelihood changed only by -1.14e-13, numerically confirming semantic label non-identifiability under full permutation symmetry.
design.memory_controllers: Posterior-driven dormant-memory controller attached to a fast PAST/GROUSE-like one-dimensional subspace tracker and a slower Oja-like tracker. Threshold/blend were calibrated on disjoint streams, then evaluated on 6 held-out seeds/scenario, 1500 steps/seed.

matched.interpretation: Adaptive duration learning gives up some performance relative to a correctly specified fixed HSMM, but remains better than duration-blind/capped controls in the matched regime.

abrupt_duration_swap.interpretation: Identity-gated duration adaptation removes most of the catastrophic stale-duration penalty, but a duration-blind HMM is statistically indistinguishable in this bounded abrupt-swap setup.

prototype_crossing.interpretation: The current adaptive duration controller fails when its independent semantic prototypes cross. Duration adaptation cannot compensate for a lost semantic anchor and can amplify label drift.

class_prior_shift.interpretation: Adaptive event-type priors help versus blind/capped controls, but stable, informative durations leave the fixed HSMM competitive.

mixed.interpretation: When duration semantics, prototype identity, and event prior all change together, all non-oracle semantic models collapse toward chance-like cause inference. The oracle gap is large, so the failure is inference/identity rather than raw observation impossibility.

posthoc_semantic_abstention_probe.scope: Exploratory post-processing only; not part of the main filter and not calibrated as a deployable rule.
posthoc_semantic_abstention_probe.interpretation: Explicitly abstaining toward 0.5 when semantic identity confidence is weak can substantially reduce damage under crossing/mixed nonstationarity, but an uncalibrated guard harms the matched regime. A principled symmetry/identifiability detector is required.

calibration.note: Calibrated on disjoint matched/abrupt/prototype-crossing streams; held-out results below use fixed calibration.

prototype_crossing.interpretation: Memory still helps reacquire a temporarily silent direction, but semantic misidentification restores stale directions after true switches and creates significant interference.

mixed.interpretation: Recovery gain and stale-memory harm cancel; no net improvement is resolved.

oja_like_slow_tracker.interpretation: The slow tracker already carries substantial inertia; adding dormant-memory restoration is counterproductive even when cause inference is good. Memory admission must be tracker-timescale-specific.

mechanistic_interpretation.positive: Explicit state-duration statistics are useful only while semantic cause identity is independently anchored. In stable-prototype duration drift, adaptive duration learning removes the large penalty of stale fixed priors. Dormant subspace memory can help a fast tracker recover from genuine temporary silence.
mechanistic_interpretation.negative_boundary: When semantic prototypes cross, duration adaptation itself becomes unsafe: the model can confidently attach the right duration to the wrong semantic label. Under simultaneous prototype/duration/prior changes, semantic labels become effectively non-identifiable and posterior-driven memory causes stale interference. Slow Oja-like trackers need little or no extra dormant-memory restoration.
mechanistic_interpretation.neuroscience_connection: Courellis et al. provide biological evidence that context identity can be represented in a comparatively static code in one circuit while other representations are dynamic. This motivates, but does not prove, an architecture in which stable semantic identity anchors condition duration priors and memory retention.

limits: Synthetic linear-Gaussian semantic emissions and one-dimensional subspace tracking; no exact SPLiT reproduction.
Prototype prediction uses a simple momentum tracker, not a fully learned neural latent-cause model.
Held-out sample counts are exploratory (8 seeds/filter scenario; 6 seeds/memory scenario).
The post-hoc semantic abstention guard was not independently calibrated and should not be treated as a finished mechanism.
Public S1 Code.zip remains unrecovered at file level.
bounded_audit.exact_next_action: Continue read-only SPLiT S1 Code.zip recovery without mutation. Replace the current prototype-separation heuristic with an explicit semantic identifiability/permutation detector: maintain multiple prototype-assignment hypotheses or a label-symmetry score, and force semantic abstention/shared-duration hazard whenever S/C assignments are observationally permutation-equivalent. Calibrate the abstention rule on disjoint matched streams so it preserves matched-regime performance, then retest prototype crossing and mixed duration/prototype/prior swaps with larger held-out seeds. Upgrade the prediction/emission anchor to a Kalman-like drifting-prototype model and test gradual crossings, unequal velocities, partial identity cues, and exact cue loss/recovery. Feed the guarded posterior into fast PAST/GROUSE-like and slow Oja-like dormant-memory controllers with tracker-specific admission/restore policies; require net improvement in both post-silence recovery and post-switch interference before retaining memory. Preserve exact scope and a nonempty frontier.
